title: Deprecate legacy checkpoint parsers and add unified weight index
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: Our model loader supports multiple legacy checkpoint parsers and ad-hoc shard metadata formats. This has caused repeated bugs during model onboarding (wrong weight ordering, tokenizer-vocab mismatches) and unpredictable memory use during warmup. The proliferation of parsing code also makes it costly to add new format features (e.g., sparse tensors, new quantized layouts). Goal: remove multiple legacy parsers by introducing a single canonical weight index file format and a compatibility layer that maps legacy manifests into the canonical index at ingest time. Implement lazy weight mapping (mmap-friendly index), explicit sharding metadata, and a tokenizer handshake that verifies vocab/hash compatibility before full load.
background: Over the last 18 months we've accumulated three parser implementations: legacy-pyckpt, shard-ledger, and ad-hoc loader. Onboarding incidents (see incident-OUTAGE-2025-11) and multiple PRs fixing weight-order bugs show this is a recurring failure mode. Earlier efforts (ENG-15876, ENG-14102) split loader responsibilities but left format compatibility unresolved. A canonical index simplifies kernel selection, enables predictable memory mapping, and lets us perform cheap validation during canary model uploads.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical weight index spec exists and is checked into docs (confluence RFC link provided)
A compatibility converter runs at model ingest to produce the canonical index for legacy checkpoints
Model loader uses the index for weight placement and exposes a lazy mmap-backed path for large tensors
Tokenizer handshake verifies token-vocab hash and fails fast with clear error messages if incompatible
End-to-end integration tests covering 5 representative legacy formats pass in CI
New index path is feature-flagged and can be rolled back safely
work_items: Draft canonical weight index spec and mapping rules (PRD + confluence RFC)
Implement converter module: legacy -> canonical index
Implement lazy index-backed loader path with mmap fallback
Add tokenizer handshake step to loader with hash check and auto-fix hints
Create integration test matrix across 5 legacy checkpoint samples and 3 shard topologies
Benchmark cold/warm startup and peak memory comparing old vs new loader
Feature-flag rollout, canary in staging, gradual production rollout plan
risks: Converter may mis-map edge-case custom shard layouts—need golden-checksums and model samples
Performance regressions if mmap path performs poorly on certain cloud filesystems
Auto-conversion increases ingest time; must be accounted for in upload UX and SLA
Tokenizer handshake could block backward-compatible clients if vocab-hash formats differ
mitigations: Collect a set of canonical model samples from infra and partners before converter implementation
Run mmap microbenchmarks on GCS/S3/EFS and implement an in-memory fallback for small models
Expose conversion progress and async conversion API for large uploads
Support a lenient tokenizer-compat mode behind a feature flag and log compatibility warnings
testing_plan: Unit tests for converter mapping rules, fuzz tests generating random shard manifests, integration tests that load converted models into runtime-1.22 in staging with synthetic traffic, and performance benchmarks measuring cold start, token-per-second, and resident memory. Add a CI job to validate index spec against committed examples.
comments: 2026-02-22 Miguel Torres: Spiked a converter prototype that maps legacy-pyckpt -> index. Found cases where legacy header misses dtype; added heuristic to infer dtype from block sizes.
2026-02-25 Aisha Khan: Reviewed prototype. Concerned about heuristic—we should prefer failing loudly unless user opts into 'best-effort' conversion. Marked as design decision to add opt-in flag.
2026-03-02 Priya Desai (Reviewer): Requested explicit schema validation and a golden set of model manifests. Also asked for clear user-facing error messages when conversion fails.

2026-03-08 Miguel Torres: Benchmarks in staging show 12% lower resident memory with lazy mmap on large 40B model, cold ingest time increased by ~9% due to conversion work. Plan: async conversion for uploads > 20GB.
2026-03-11 Jin Park (SRE): Noted that mmap path on NFS instances had 30% slower page faults. Agreed to detect NFS and fallback to eager load for such mounts.
